question.:question/problem:
What is the center and radius of the circle with equation $$
\displaystyle (x-\frac{5}{3})^{2}+(y+\frac{7}{2})^{2}=72?
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Let's compare the general equation to our equation side-by-side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-\frac{5}{3})^{2}+(y+\frac{7}{2})^{2} & =72 \\ (x-\frac{5}{3})^{2}+(y-\left(- \frac{7}{2}\right))^{2} & =(6 \sqrt{2})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The radius is the positive square root of the right-hand side:

$$
r=\sqrt{72}=\sqrt{36\cdot 2}=6 \sqrt{2}.
$$

We see that $a=\frac{5}{3},$ $b=- \frac{7}{2},$ and $r=6 \sqrt{2}.$ 

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(\frac{5}{3},- \frac{7}{2})$ and its radius is $6 \sqrt{2}.$
